title: Macy's Let Its Giant Balloons Fly Away
sources: Untapped New York, 'Thanksgiving Day Parade balloon release': from 1928 until 1932 the giant balloons were released at the end of the route; rewards for returned balloons; 1928 tiger balloon ripped to pieces on a Richmond Hill roof; 1932 aviation student Annette Gibson flew into the Tom-Cat balloon over Queens, it wrapped her left wing, the plane went into a tailspin and instructor Hugh Copeland recovered it; this ended the releases

Mental Floss, '16 Fun Facts About the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade': 1928 balloons released with a $100 reward for whoever returned them; a tug of war over one on a Long Island roof; one landed in the East River and was pursued by tugboats; last balloon release in 1932
Smithsonian Magazine, 'The Puppeteer Who Brought Balloons to the Thanksgiving Day Parade'

lines.text: Macy's once let its giant parade balloons fly away, on purpose.
